QUESTION: What is posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PT-Cy), and what transplant problem is it used to overcome, in which donor settings?

ATOM: Posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PT-Cy) is a pharmacological strategy used to overcome human leukocyte antigen (HLA) barriers in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) from haploidentical donors, and more recently in matched donor transplants.
KEY POINTS:
1. Pharmacological strategy (cyclophosphamide given after transplant) to overcome HLA barriers in allogeneic HCT
2. Used in haploidentical donor transplants and, more recently, in matched donor transplants

ANSWER TO GRADE:
Posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PT-Cy) is high-dose cyclophosphamide given shortly after an allogeneic blood stem-cell transplant to eliminate rapidly proliferating alloreactive T cells. It reduces graft-versus-host disease and graft rejection, helping overcome HLA mismatch in haploidentical related and mismatched unrelated donor transplants; it is also used with matched donors.
